purpose: The launch Catalog. `items` are what the Catalog screen lists, `recipes` hold every Recipe that is not a plain Homebrew install, plus the Base Items and settings. An Item with no entry in `recipes` gets its Recipe from `install`.

homebrew.note: Official JSON was downloaded before this file was built. check.py downloads it again. Tap files were read from GitHub on the same day. Nothing was installed.

sections.name: Languages and runtimes
sections.summary: Runtimes sit with their language. A version manager for one language sits in that language's group. mise and asdf sit together because each one covers many languages.

sections.name: Browsers
sections.summary: One group. Safari ships with macOS and is not an Item.

sections.name: Editors and IDEs
sections.summary: Editors people open as the main coding window, including JetBrains IDEs. An editor whose main window is an agent is in Agentic development.

sections.name: Agentic development
sections.summary: Agentic editors are full editors built around an agent. Agent CLIs are terminal programs. Chat apps and local model runners are separate groups so they are not mistaken for the coding agent.

sections.name: Terminals and shells
sections.summary: Terminal apps, shells other than the system zsh, a prompt, and multiplexers.

sections.name: CLI tools
sections.summary: Small tools that show up in most developer setups. Language servers, niche search tools, and extra system monitors are left out.

sections.name: Containers and virtual machines
sections.summary: Container engines are one group because they overlap. Virtual machine apps are the other.

sections.name: Databases and API clients
sections.summary: Servers, desktop clients, and API clients. A server and a client for the same database are both listed.

sections.name: Git and code hosting
sections.summary: Git itself, Git clients, and host CLIs other than gh. gh is a base Item.

sections.name: Mobile development
sections.summary: Apple tools, Android tools, and tools that target both. Simulators are not separate Items.

sections.name: Cloud and infrastructure
sections.summary: Provider CLIs, Kubernetes tools, infrastructure-as-code tools, and platform CLIs.

sections.name: Networking
sections.summary: VPN and tunnels, then traffic inspection. Tailscale is the Standalone app.

sections.name: Window management and utilities
sections.summary: Window layout, launchers, menu bar and input tools, and screenshot tools.

sections.name: Communication and design
sections.summary: Chat, notes, design, and password managers that developers commonly install.

sections.name: Fonts
sections.summary: Monospaced fonts for code. One Nerd Font build is included.
